summary.headline: Aarti Pharmalabs Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 42% YoY to INR535 crore, PAT up 49% to INR71 crore, led by record Xanthine sales.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue reached INR535 crore (up 42% YoY) with EBITDA of INR133 crore (up 40%) and PAT of INR71 crore (up 49%). Xanthine derivatives made up 57% of turnover and hit its highest-ever quarterly sales, helped by raw-material pass-through and price increases during the West Asia crisis. CDMO/CMO fell to 7% of revenue, with management attributing this to postponed deliveries and expecting H2-weighted growth. Management said Xanthine prices have eased from peaks in June-July, so the company expects a lower realisation per kg going forward.

financial_highlights.metric: Gross margin (company level, as cited by analyst)
financial_highlights.change: Management indicated ~50% plus or minus a few points as sustainable
Highest-ever quarterly Xanthine sales; volume up ~25% YoY per management
Below INR200 crore quarterly run-rate of Q4 FY25
Guidance of 40-50% growth for FY27, H2-weighted

segments.name: Xanthine derivatives
segments.commentary: 57% of Q1 turnover; 74% beverage customers, 26% others; exports 79%, local 21%. Volume up ~25% YoY; realisation per kg expected to decline in Q2. FY27 Xanthine sales guided at INR900-1,000 crore (range INR900-1,100 crore).

segments.name: API & Intermediates
segments.commentary: 30% of turnover; 58% regulated markets, 14% rest of world, 28% non-regulated. Steroid block debottlenecking (+33% capacity) caused ~1.5-month shutdown in Q1; pricing pressure on existing molecules. Gross margin ~45-50%.

segments.name: CDMO/CMO
segments.commentary: 7% of revenue; 22 customers, 57 active projects (37 commercial, 20 development). Management reiterated 40-50% FY27 growth, H2-weighted, and INR1,000 crore revenue target (FY29-30).

segments.name: Others
segments.commentary: 6% of turnover, comprising scrap sales, trading sales (group buying of solvents) and export incentives; management described it as low margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone EBITDA margin guided at 22-25%; company-level EBITDA range of 20-25% cited, and gross margin ~50% plus or minus a few points.
Xanthine FY27 revenue range INR900-1,100 crore, with management leaning to INR900-1,000 crore depending on price normalisation.
CDMO/CMO growth of 40-50% in FY27, H2-weighted; CDMO expected to reach ~20% of revenue this year and 25-30% of sales over time.
API revenue targeted near last year's ~INR780 crore level; management expects to be 'nearly there' rather than crossing it. Steroid debottlenecking implies ~INR170-190 crore quarterly API run-rate.
Xanthine target 20-25% global market share in next two years; utilisation of 80%+ by FY28.
capex_capacity: Steroid block debottlenecking at Unit 4, Tarapur (USFDA-approved) completed in Q1 FY27, adding 33% to steroidal capacity.
Xanthine brownfield site (L99) capacity commercialised by end-Q1; trial production ongoing. Capacity rising from ~6,000 MT to ~9,500 MT over the next couple of years.
Atali Block 1 (440 kL reactor capacity) both phases to be fully operational in Q2 FY27; pre-operating expenses to hit books in H2 FY27.
Atali Block 2 dedicated CDMO block: INR149 crore capex, 400+ kL (405 kL approved, +200 kL civil-ready). Groundbreaking Q3 FY27, completion in 12-15 months (end FY28 start of operations).
Anticancer Block 3 debottlenecking ongoing; Block 5 has an additional line. Management says no further capex needed for INR1,000 crore API ambition.
demand_pricing: Xanthine raw-material costs rose 50-100% during the West Asia crisis; by end-June and July they eased to roughly 25-50% above prior levels. Management says prices are still above pre-war levels.

China removed Xanthine export rebates and imposed production quota cuts (anti-involution policy), which management says structurally supports Xanthine prices. Management splits the price increase roughly 50-50 between structural and temporary.
Price pass-through contracts with large customers; spot-market prices expected to fall. Management says Q1 was 'exceptional' for top line.

API pricing pressure on existing molecules from launches; cost-reduction and process intensification projects underway. Top 10 API products are 60-70% of API sales, with 10-50% market share in those molecules.
CDMO: 37 commercial projects, up from 21 three years ago; one new customer and three net new projects added in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Xanthine volume vs realisation growth YoY, and Q2 realisation trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume up ~25% YoY. Realisation per kg expected to decline in Q2 as supply chains normalise, though sales will grow with added capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 gross margin of ~56% sustainable given falling Xanthine realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said absolute gross margin should be sustained as higher volumes from ~9,500 MT capacity offset lower prices; company-level gross margin ~50% plus or minus a few points.

qa_highlights.question: Is CDMO revenue H2-heavy this year and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, FY27 CDMO will be H2-heavy as in prior years; 40-50% growth reiterated. Net +3 projects and +1 customer in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CDMO revenue fall to 7% in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited postponed sales due to non-deliveries under accounting standards; expects to build up over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Can Xanthine FY27 revenue reach INR1,100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave a range of INR900-1,100 crore, leaning to INR900-1,000 crore, depending on price normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Xanthine price rise structural or temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Involution-driven changes are seen as structural for the next few years; raw-material spikes as temporary. Management said roughly 50-50 split.

qa_highlights.question: What would API revenue have been without the steroid shutdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated INR170-190 crore per quarter, with the shutdown having reduced Q1 revenue.
